CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine

PATIENT: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
SEX: Female

ORDERING PHYSICIAN: Dr. [redacted name]
DATE COLLECTED: [redacted date]
DATE RECEIVED: [redacted date]
DATE REPORTED: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for referral: Patient with splenomegaly, evaluated for possible myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) or multiple myeloma (MM)

SPECIMEN TYPE
Bone marrow aspirate

TEST PERFORMED
Conventional cytogenetic analysis (karyotype)

METHODOLOGY
Bone marrow cells were cultured for 24 and 48 hours without mitogens. Metaphase chromosomes were prepared using standard techniques and analyzed by G-banding at a resolution of 400-550 bands. Twenty metaphase cells were analyzed and karyotyped according to the International System for Human Cytogenomic Nomenclature (ISCN 2020).

RESULTS
Karyotype: 46,XX[20]

Normal female karyotype (46,XX) in all 20 analyzed cells. No clonal chromosomal abnormalities detected.

INTERPRETATION
Conventional cytogenetic analysis revealed a normal female karyotype with no evidence of chromosomal abnormalities. No abnormal clone was detected by G-banding analysis. These findings do not support a diagnosis of myeloproliferative neoplasm based on cytogenetic criteria.

While this normal karyotype does not exclude the possibility of MPN or MM, many cases of these disorders may have normal conventional cytogenetics. Molecular studies (e.g., JAK2, CALR, MPL mutations for MPN) or FISH analysis may provide additional diagnostic information.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Correlation with morphologic findings, flow cytometry, and molecular studies is recommended for comprehensive evaluation of suspected MPN.
2. If final diagnosis is multiple myeloma with >10% plasma cells in bone marrow, consider FISH analysis for myeloma-associated abnormalities including del(13q), del(17p), t(4;14), t(11;14), t(14;16), and 1q21 amplification.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
